themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge This Week
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 80 THIS WEEK, up 288% from the 8-week average of 20.6 complaints per week—a statistically significant surge (z-score: 6.15) that suggests a sudden, localized noise source or event affecting outdoor areas in St. George/Stapleton.
evidence: 80 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 20.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (288% spike, z-score 6.15)
Noise complaints overall up 140% three weeks ago (33 vs. 13.8 avg), but street/sidewalk category only spiked THIS WEEK
This is the most recent and most statistically severe spike in the dataset, appearing only in the current week
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks to identify the source: construction, commercial activity, venue, or traffic pattern change
Interview residents in high-complaint areas about when the noise started and whether it's tied to a specific project or business

themes_detail.label: Water System Crisis Escalating
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints surged to 113 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 171% from the 8-week average of 41.8 per week (z-score: 4.03)—a statistically significant spike suggesting widespread service disruptions, main breaks, or water quality issues affecting multiple households.
evidence: 113 water system complaints two weeks ago vs. 41.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (171% spike, z-score 4.03)
Water system ranked 9th among all complaint types over 90 days (647 total), indicating chronic baseline issue now acute
Long-running community board request for 'Other capital budget request for DEP' suggests systemic water infrastructure problems
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP to determine whether a main break, service outage, or water quality event occurred two weeks ago and affected this district
Interview affected residents about service disruptions: were homes without water, low pressure, or discolored water?
Cross-reference with historical data to determine whether this is an isolated incident or part of a pattern of water infrastructure failures

themes_detail.label: Street Signs Disappearing/Damaged
themes_detail.summary: Missing street signs jumped to 5 complaints LAST WEEK, up 344% from 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 6.46), and damaged street signs also hit 5 complaints LAST WEEK, up 264% from 1.4 average—a combined infrastructure failure affecting wayfinding and traffic safety.
evidence: 5 missing street sign complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (344% spike, z-score 6.46)
5 damaged street sign complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (264% spike, z-score 4.23)
Long-standing community board request for 'Repair or provide new street lights' indicates existing DOT maintenance gaps in this district
reporting_angles: Walk the district to identify clusters of missing or damaged street signs and photograph locations
File a FOIL request with DOT to determine whether a weather event, contractor work, or theft triggered the spike last week
Interview DOT about response timeline and whether the district is understaffed for street furniture maintenance

themes_detail.label: Dumpster and Lot Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints exploded to 8 THREE WEEKS AGO, up 1500% from 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 10.61, highest severity in dataset), and dumpster complaints hit 5 LAST WEEK, up 700% from 0.6 average—suggesting acute sanitation failures affecting outdoor spaces and waste management.
evidence: 8 lot condition complaints three weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score 10.61—highest severity in entire dataset)
5 dumpster complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 4.41)
Lot and dumpster issues both indicate neglected outdoor spaces and potential environmental health hazards
reporting_angles: Identify which lots and dumpster locations generated complaints and assess current conditions on the ground
Determine whether complaints relate to a single property owner, contractor neglect, or lack of city enforcement
Interview sanitation and code enforcement to understand why these specific locations are failing and what corrective action is underway

themes_detail.label: Special Projects Inspection Team Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints hit 3 THREE WEEKS AGO, up 700% from 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting heightened building code or quality-of-life enforcement activity, possibly tied to illegal conversions or property violations.
evidence: 3 SPIT complaints three weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Community board has long-standing budget request to 'Address illegal conversions and uses of buildings,' indicating known enforcement need
SPIT activity suggests DOB or city enforcement action; timing and scope requires clarification
reporting_angles: Contact DOB to learn what triggered the SPIT deployment three weeks ago and which properties/complaints were involved
Cross-reference with DOB permit data (642 total filings in last 90 days, 444 alterations) to identify whether enforcement is linked to unpermitted work
